name: Encaje
description: Encaje, also known as Mus Francés (French Mus), is a version of the Basque game Mus adapted for 3 or 5 players. Unlike standard Mus, Encaje is played without partnerships—each player competes individually. The unique twist is that there is no winner, only a loser; the goal is to avoid being the last player with stones remaining.

content.text: Encaje, also known as Mus Francés (French Mus), is a version of the Basque game Mus adapted for 3 or 5 players. Unlike standard Mus, Encaje is played without partnerships—each player competes individually. The unique twist is that there is no winner, only a loser; the goal is to avoid being the last player with stones remaining.

Country/Region of Origin: Spain/Basque Country
Time Period: Early 20th century
Historical Development: Evolved from the traditional Basque game Mus as a variant for odd numbers of players
Cultural Significance: Popular in Basque regions and among Mus enthusiasts who want to play with 3 or 5 players

Minimum Players: 3
Maximum Players: 5
Optimal Players: 5
Partnerships: None (individual play)

Type: Spanish 40-card deck (without 8s, 9s, 10s)
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included

Spanish 40-card deck
Stones or tokens (15-21 per player)
Score tracking system

Two methods available:
1. Standard deal: 4 cards to each player, with 'mus' round for exchanging cards
2. Alternative deal: 5 cards to each player, each discards 1 face down before betting
Deal rotates anticlockwise
